The public universe appears sparse for pure-play product information management, digital shelf analytics, review syndication, and marketplace feed management; several prominent vendors found in search context, including Salsify, Syndigo, Bazaarvoice, PowerReviews, CommerceIQ, and Rithum, are not obvious US-listed pure plays.

memory_update.text: SPSC should be carried forward as the highest-fit underfollowed candidate for retail data plumbing: fulfillment compliance, catalog-aligned analytics, inventory/sales data, and trading-partner network effects.

CRTO should be carried forward as the retail-media and sponsored-product visibility candidate; key gate is whether commerce media growth is measurable and durable enough to offset legacy ad-tech risks.
RAMP should be tracked as a second-order retail-media clean-room and data-collaboration infrastructure candidate, not as direct product-content infrastructure.
YEXT is a speculative-shadow candidate for AI search/entity/discovery data; it needs proof of product-level ecommerce workflows before surviving later Serenity layers.

Pure public exposure to PIM, review syndication, digital shelf analytics, and marketplace content syndication appears limited; later passes should map private leaders and public acquirers/owners to avoid false purity assumptions.

For this node, the likely public-stock chokepoint may be less about AI model vendors and more about operational data rails: product catalog accuracy, retail trading rules, inventory availability, retail-media measurement, and permissioned brand-retailer data collaboration.

node: AI-mediated shopping, retail data and product-content infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B expanded the public-stock universe for the scarce-provider side of AI-mediated shopping and retail data infrastructure. The strongest public candidates are not pure PIM/digital-shelf vendors because many core vendors in product content, review syndication, and marketplace optimization appear private or embedded inside larger ad-tech/commerce stacks. The public chokepoint lane therefore clusters around retail trading-network data, commerce-media platforms, retail-media data collaboration, and AI-search/discovery data management. No investment recommendation is implied.
